values.note: Basic sites only: $15 a night in season, $5 less mid-October through April. Pay at the self-service box. Plus tax and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year).

note: Small Sandhills SRA on a 60-acre lake near Merriman: 30 basic grass sites in clusters around the north and west shores, a water hydrant May 1 - October 1, and vault toilets; no dump station. Campers report small sites and a tight turnaround at the back (a 32-ft Class C found one paved, level site in the first section, 2022). Register at the self-service box. --Claude
summary: Confirmed basic-only and first come, $15 in season / $10 off-season (2025 grid, July 2025 camper report). Raises a fit question from camper reviews. Waterfront lakefront is not confirmed by imagery (a lead, possibly down). No sand-driving evidence. Pin is on the boat-ramp peninsula.
flags: FIT QUESTION (23-ft motorhome): Campendium camper-631595, September 11, 2022: 'In the first section as you pull in we found 1 paved site for our 32 ft class C and it was level!' and 'The turn around at the back of the campground was tight, did have to back up a couple times to make the turn.' Gypsy-Woman2, July 08, 2020: 'No place to park a Class C or bigger, I barely got turned around.' and 'Sites were for tents really unless you camp with a van or pickup camper.' Lurik, August 26, 2021: 'Sites were small.' A 32-ft rig did fit one site, so I read this as keep with a caveat (now in the note), not a drop. No official site-length figure exists (not on ReserveAmerica; outdoornebraska.gov blocked).

SAND RULE: no evidence of driving onto sand or beach. Not on ReserveAmerica, so there is no 'Driveway Surface'. Imagery shows gravel/dirt park roads through grass and trees (NGPC 2019: 'paved entrance road'), and the camping clusters sit on grass. The sand rim visible around the lake is a bare shoreline with no tracks to it. One camper calls the access a 'Washboard road in terrible condition' (2020). Sandhills soil means soft shoulders are possible; that is unverified.

WATERFRONT LEAD (possibly down, lakefront -> lakeview): the NGPC page (quoted by a search summary only; outdoornebraska.gov is blocked) says the 30 sites are 'located along the shoreline'. A Dyrt review (Oct. 30, 2026) says 'right on the lake'. On NAIP/Esri, however, individual pads can't be resolved. The two treed camping clusters measure ~75-85 m from open water: the WEST cluster (~42.9146,-101.6794) is behind a cattail/marsh margin and trees, and the NORTH cluster of campers on open grass (~42.9164,-101.6762) is ~75 m from the north lobe. Only the grassy boat-ramp peninsula at the pin is ~30 m from water, and no pads are visible there. The stored evidence is only the 2026-06 sweep commit pointer. I couldn't confirm on-water pads, so the rules point down to lakeview unless an official site map shows shoreline pads.

PIN: stored 42.91425,-101.67581 is on the boat-ramp/parking peninsula at the end of the park road, ~250-300 m from the west camping cluster and ~240 m from the north one. No move proposed, because I can't see the pads well enough to give a better point; a camping-area centre would be ~42.9152,-101.6777.

WEBSITE: the stored second line is visitnebraska.com, a tourism directory (Cloudflare-blocked); the NGPC page https://outdoornebraska.gov/location/cottonwood-lake/ is the operator's page and should stay.
